### `SharedPoll`

Signatures for shared poll subscriptions.

See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/shared_poll. Shared poll
subscriptions are experimental in Centrifugo, and this class follows their
changes.

#### `static sign(
    string $secret,
    string $user,
    string $channel,
    array $keys,
    ?DateTimeInterface $expiresAt = null,
): string`

The signature authorizing $user to track $keys in $channel until
$expiresAt, as Centrifugo verifies it: "iat:exp:hmac", iat now and exp
$expiresAt in Unix seconds - 0 when $expiresAt is null, for a signature
which does not expire. $secret is Centrifugo's
shared_poll.hmac_secret_key; $user is the ID of the connection's user,
empty for an anonymous one.

The signature covers exactly $keys, in their order: a client tracking
other keys, or the same in another order, is refused. Name the
arguments, so that a user and a channel cannot be swapped:

```php
SharedPoll::sign($secret, user: '42', channel: 'poll:prices', keys: ['AAPL'], expiresAt: $exp);
```

## Centrifugal\Phpcent\Exception

Every exception implements `CentException`.

- `ApiException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
  - `BadRequestException`
- `BatchFailedCommandsException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
- `BatchNotSentException` (a `\LogicException`)
- `BatchSentException` (a `\LogicException`)
- `BroadcastFailedChannelsException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
- `CentException`
- `ClosedException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
  - `ConflictException`
- `DecodeException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
- `HttpException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
  - `InternalException`
- `InvalidConfigException` (a `\InvalidArgumentException`)
- `InvalidRequestException` (a `\InvalidArgumentException`)
- `NetworkException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
  - `NotAvailableException`
  - `NotFoundException`
- `TimeoutException` (a `\RuntimeException`)
  - `TooManyRequestsException`
  - `UnauthorizedException`
  - `UnknownChannelException`
  - `UnrecoverablePositionException`

### `ApiException`

```php
new ApiException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

An error of Centrifugo itself: it understood the request and refused it, or
failed to carry it out.

Centrifugo identifies an error by its code - getCode() - while its message
is for people and may change. Errors with a known code are thrown as the
subclass for it - catch UnknownChannelException - and any other code as
ApiException itself: Centrifugo adds codes from time to time, so match the
ones you handle and treat the rest by their class.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

#### `static fromCode(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
): ApiException`

The exception for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiException otherwise.

### `BadRequestException`

```php
new BadRequestException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 107: Centrifugo refused the request as invalid.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `BatchFailedCommandsException`

```php
new BatchFailedCommandsException(array $failed, int $total, BatchResult $result)
```

A batch in which one or more commands failed, up to all of them. Every
command got its own reply: each Pending holds its outcome. $result is the
batch's.

It is not an ApiException of its parts: look at each command's error in
$failed, or at its Pending.

- `$failed` `list<FailedCommand>`

### `BatchNotSentException`

```php
new BatchNotSentException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

A pending command's result read before its batch was sent.

### `BatchSentException`

```php
new BatchSentException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

A batch sent again: a batch is sent once.

### `BroadcastFailedChannelsException`

```php
new BroadcastFailedChannelsException(array $failed, int $total, BroadcastResult $result)
```

A broadcast Centrifugo carried out which failed in one or more of its
channels, up to all of them. $result holds every channel's outcome.

It is not an ApiException of its parts: catch (UnknownChannelException) does
not catch a broadcast in which one channel of many was unknown, nor one into
a single channel - the broadcast as a whole is not unknown. Look at each
channel's error in $failed.

- `$failed` `list<ChannelResult>` - the channels which failed, with their errors, in the order of the request
- `$total` `int` - how many channels the broadcast had
- `$result` `BroadcastResult` - every channel's outcome

#### `retryableChannels(): list<string>`

The channels whose failure is retryable, in the order of the request: the
channels a retry should go to, with the same idempotencyKey. Channels
which failed for good, such as an unknown channel, are left out.

### interface `CentException`

Implemented by every exception phpcent throws: catch CentException for all of
them.

### `ClosedException`

```php
new ClosedException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

A call made after the client was closed.

### `ConflictException`

```php
new ConflictException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 113: the request conflicts with the current state - a map publish whose
version check failed, say.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `DecodeException`

```php
new DecodeException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

The reply is not a Centrifugo API reply. The usual cause is an apiEndpoint
which does not point at Centrifugo's API, so that something else - a proxy,
a web page - answers instead.

### `HttpException`

```php
new HttpException(int $statusCode, string $body = '', array $headers = [], string $proMethod = '')
```

A reply with an HTTP status other than 200: the request did not reach the API
method. A 401 is an UnauthorizedException.

- `$statusCode` `int` - the reply's HTTP status
- `$body` `string` - the start of the reply's body, for diagnostics
- `$headers` `array<string, string>` - the reply's headers, names in lower case: a request ID a proxy set, a Retry-After
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which got a 404, for the hint in the message

#### `static fromStatus(
    int $statusCode,
    string $body = '',
    array $headers = [],
    string $proMethod = '',
): HttpException`

### `InternalException`

```php
new InternalException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 100: an internal error of Centrifugo, temporary.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `InvalidConfigException`

```php
new InvalidConfigException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

A configuration with a mistake: the message names the option and the fix.

### `InvalidRequestException`

```php
new InvalidRequestException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

A request the client can tell is wrong without sending it: one which cannot be
encoded - a payload which is not JSON, in any request - or a publication
without a channel or data. It is never sent.

Only rules which hold for every Centrifugo are checked; everything else
Centrifugo checks itself, and reports as a BadRequestException.

### `NetworkException`

```php
new NetworkException(string $message, bool $certificate = false, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

The request failed on its way: a refused or reset connection, a failed TLS
handshake. The cause, when there is one, is the previous exception.

- `$certificate` `bool` - the server's TLS certificate was refused, which no retry fixes

### `NotAvailableException`

```php
new NotAvailableException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 108: the feature is not available - history or presence off in the
channel's namespace, say.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `NotFoundException`

```php
new NotFoundException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 104: what the request refers to was not found.

A method only Centrifugo PRO has, sent in a batch to Centrifugo OSS, fails
with it too, instead of the 404 it gets when sent alone.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `TimeoutException`

```php
new TimeoutException(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

The request timed out: its timeout, or requestTimeout. A request which timed
out may still have been carried out.

### `TooManyRequestsException`

```php
new TooManyRequestsException(
    int $code,
    string $serverMessage = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    string $proMethod = '',
)
```

Code 111: a rate limit was reached, temporary.

- `$code` `int` - Centrifugo's error code
- `$serverMessage` `string` - Centrifugo's message, for people
- `$temporary` `bool` - set by Centrifugo when the same request may succeed if retried later - a broker being unavailable, a rate limit - not because of the request. It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which failed with code 104 in a batch, for the hint in the message

### `UnauthorizedException`

```php
new UnauthorizedException(
    int $statusCode,
    string $body = '',
    array $headers = [],
    string $proMethod = '',

```

A 401: Centrifugo did not accept the credentials - the API key or the bearer

- `$headers` `array<string, string>` - the reply's headers, names in lower case: a request ID a proxy set, a Retry-After
- `$proMethod` `string` - a Centrifugo PRO method which got a 404, for the hint in the message

Code 102: the channel is not in a namespace Centrifugo is configured with.

It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.

It does not mean nothing was done: a publication may have happened, so retry it with the same idempotencyKey. Centrifugo versions before the field existed never set it; Retry::retryable takes that into account.

## Centrifugal\Phpcent\Token

### `ApiClaims`

```php
new ApiClaims(
    string $audience = '',
    array $scope = [],
    string $issuer = '',
    string $subject = '',
    ?DateTimeInterface $expiresAt = null,
    ?DateTimeInterface $issuedAt = null,
    string $id = '',
)
```

The claims of a token authenticating calls to Centrifugo PRO's server API,
verified with the keys of http_api.jwks.endpoint. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/pro/server_api_enhancements.

A token passing Centrifugo PRO's checks can call every API method, and it
checks only what it is configured to: the signature by any key of the JWKS
endpoint, and audience, issuer and scope only when http_api.jwks sets them.
So the token must carry a claim no other token carries - above all the
connection and subscription tokens users hold:

- sign API tokens with keys of their own, published at their own JWKS
  endpoint - never the one of client.token.jwks_public_endpoint;
- set audience, scope or both, to values only API tokens carry, and
  configure http_api.jwks.audience and scope to require them. Token::api
  refuses claims with neither.

- `$audience` `string` - the "aud" claim: http_api.jwks.audience
- `$scope` `list<string>` - the "scope" claim, its scopes joined by spaces: http_api.jwks.scope is one of them
- `$issuer` `string` - the "iss" claim: http_api.jwks.issuer
- `$subject` `string` - the "sub" claim: who calls the API, for the application's own logs
- `$expiresAt` `?\DateTimeInterface` - when the token expires: required by Token::api, best minutes ahead. Centrifugo PRO would accept a token without "exp" for as long as its key is published, so Token::api never signs one. ApiTokens sets it itself.
- `$issuedAt` `?\DateTimeInterface` - the "iat" claim; null for now
- `$id` `string` - the "jti" claim

### `ApiTokens`

```php
new ApiTokens(ApiClaims $claims, ?Key $key = null, ?callable $currentKey = null, float $ttl = 300.0)
```

Issues the tokens a Client sends to Centrifugo PRO: its token method is the
client's bearerTokenFunc. It signs a token with Token::api and reuses it for
half its lifetime, so a token sent has at least half of it left.

```php
$tokens = new ApiTokens(
    claims: new ApiClaims(audience: 'centrifugo-api', scope: ['centrifugo:api']),
    key: $apiKey,   // its own key, not the client tokens'
);
$client = new Client('https://centrifugo.example.com/api', bearerTokenFunc: $tokens->token(...));
```

$currentKey, when set, returns the key to sign each new token with instead of
$key - the key active now, when keys rotate. A key must be published in the
JWKS before it signs: Centrifugo PRO refuses a token whose key it can't
find. $claims must leave expiresAt and issuedAt unset: the tokens are issued
when needed and expire $ttl seconds later (300 by default).

- `$currentKey` `?callable(): Key`

#### `token(): string`

A token valid for at least half of ttl, signing a new one when the previous one has less left.

### `ChannelsCapability`

```php
new ChannelsCapability(array $channels = [], array $allow = [], string $match = '')
```

Operations granted in channels: a connection may do an operation in a channel
when any of its capabilities allows the operation and matches the channel.
Centrifugo PRO only.

- `$channels` `list<string>` - the channels, or channel patterns, it applies to
- `$allow` `list<string>` - the operations: "sub" (subscribe), "pub" (publish), "hst" (history), "prs" (presence)
- `$match` `string` - how channels are matched: empty for exact names, "wildcard" or "regex"

### `ConnectionClaims`

```php
new ConnectionClaims(
    DateTimeInterface|Expiry $expiresAt,
    string $user = '',
    DateTimeInterface|Expiry|null $connectionExpiresAt = null,
    ?DateTimeInterface $issuedAt = null,
    string $id = '',
    string $audience = '',
    string $issuer = '',
    mixed $info = null,
    string $b64info = '',
    array $channels = [],
    array $subs = [],
    mixed $meta = null,
    array $caps = [],
    array $labels = [],
)
```

The claims of a connection token. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/authentication.

- `$expiresAt` `\DateTimeInterface|Expiry` - until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, or Expiry::Never for a token accepted forever - and forever once leaked, for a trusted service's own connection, say. Required. The connection expires then too, unless connectionExpiresAt says otherwise: Centrifugo asks the client for a new token, and closes the connection without one.
- `$user` `string` - the ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim. Empty for an anonymous connection.
- `$connectionExpiresAt` `\DateTimeInterface|Expiry|null` - when set, when the connection expires instead of at expiresAt: the "expire_at" claim. Expiry::Never makes the connection never expire - Centrifugo never asks for a new token - while expiresAt still bounds when the token is accepted, on reconnects too. Most applications leave it unset.
- `$issuedAt` `?\DateTimeInterface` - the "iat" claim; null for now
- `$id` `string` - the "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation
- `$audience` `string` - the "aud" claim: client.token.audience
- `$issuer` `string` - the "iss" claim: client.token.issuer
- `$info` `mixed` - information about the connection: in presence, join and leave events, and the client's publications
- `$b64info` `string` - binary info in base64, instead of info
- `$channels` `list<string>` - server-side channels to subscribe the connection to
- `$subs` `array<string, SubscribeOptions>` - server-side channels to subscribe the connection to, each with its options. Set channels or subs, not both: Centrifugo ignores channels when subs is set.
- `$meta` `mixed` - custom data attached to the connection. Not visible to other clients - Centrifugo never sends it - but the token carries it, visible to the user owning the token: put nothing in it that user must not see.
- `$caps` `list<ChannelsCapability>` - capabilities granting the connection operations in channels. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `$labels` `array<string, string>` - the connection's client labels: for metrics, targeted server API calls and CEL expressions. Centrifugo PRO only.

### enum `Expiry`

An expiry chosen to be never - always explicitly: for expiresAt, a token
accepted forever, and forever once leaked; for connectionExpiresAt and
subscriptionExpiresAt, a connection or subscription which never expires.

- `Expiry::Never`

### `Key`

A key signing tokens, matching the one Centrifugo verifies with. Make one
with Key::hmac, Key::rsa, Key::ecdsa, Key::ed25519 or Key::fromPem.

HMAC keys need nothing but PHP; RSA and ECDSA keys need ext-openssl,
Ed25519 keys ext-sodium.

#### `static ecdsa(OpenSSLAsymmetricKey|string $privateKey, ?string $passphrase = null): Key`

A key signing with ES256, ES384 or ES512 - for a P-256, P-384 or P-521
key - whose public key is Centrifugo's client.token.ecdsa_public_key: an
OpenSSL key, or its PEM.

#### `static ed25519(string $privateKey): Key`

A key signing with EdDSA, whose public key is Centrifugo's
client.token.ed25519_public_key (Centrifugo v6.10.2+), or is published in
its JWKS: a 32-byte seed, or a 64-byte secret key of ext-sodium.

#### `static fromPem(string $pem, ?string $passphrase = null): Key`

The key of a PEM-encoded private key - RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519 - as
Key::rsa, Key::ecdsa or Key::ed25519 make it.

#### `static hmac(string $secret): Key`

A key signing with HS256 and $secret: Centrifugo's client.token.hmac_secret_key.

#### `static rsa(OpenSSLAsymmetricKey|string $privateKey, ?string $passphrase = null): Key`

A key signing with RS256, whose public key is Centrifugo's
client.token.rsa_public_key: an OpenSSL key, or its PEM.

#### `withKeyId(string $kid): Key`

The key, with $kid as the "kid" of the tokens it signs: the ID of its
public key in the JWKS Centrifugo verifies with. Never give the ID of a
key to another: Centrifugo caches keys by ID, and would refuse the other
key's tokens until its cache expires.

### `SubscribeOptions`

```php
new SubscribeOptions(
    mixed $info = null,
    string $b64info = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    ?SubscribeOptionOverride $override = null,
    ?FilterNode $serverTagsFilter = null,
)
```

The options of a server-side subscription in ConnectionClaims::$subs.

- `$info` `mixed` - channel-specific information about the connection
- `$b64info` `string` - binary info in base64, instead of info
- `$data` `mixed` - sent to the client with the subscription
- `$b64data` `string` - binary data in base64, instead of data
- `$override` `?SubscribeOptionOverride` - channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription
- `$serverTagsFilter` `?FilterNode` - only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only, which refuses a malformed filter: the subscription fails.

### `SubscriptionClaims`

```php
new SubscriptionClaims(
    string $channel,
    DateTimeInterface|Expiry $expiresAt,
    string $user = '',
    DateTimeInterface|Expiry|null $subscriptionExpiresAt = null,
    ?DateTimeInterface $issuedAt = null,
    string $id = '',
    string $audience = '',
    string $issuer = '',
    mixed $info = null,
    string $b64info = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    ?SubscribeOptionOverride $override = null,
    array $allow = [],
    ?FilterNode $serverTagsFilter = null,
)
```

The claims of a subscription token. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/channel_token_auth.

- `$channel` `string` - the channel the token allows to subscribe to. Required.
- `$expiresAt` `\DateTimeInterface|Expiry` - until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, or Expiry::Never. Required. The subscription expires then too, unless subscriptionExpiresAt says otherwise.
- `$user` `string` - the ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim
- `$subscriptionExpiresAt` `\DateTimeInterface|Expiry|null` - when set, when the subscription expires instead of at expiresAt: the "expire_at" claim. Expiry::Never makes it never expire, while expiresAt still bounds when the token is accepted: with a short expiresAt, a token which subscribes once.
- `$issuedAt` `?\DateTimeInterface` - the "iat" claim; null for now
- `$id` `string` - the "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation
- `$audience` `string` - the "aud" claim
- `$issuer` `string` - the "iss" claim
- `$info` `mixed` - channel-specific information about the connection
- `$b64info` `string` - binary info in base64, instead of info
- `$data` `mixed` - sent to the client in the subscribe reply
- `$b64data` `string` - binary data in base64, instead of data
- `$override` `?SubscribeOptionOverride` - channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription
- `$allow` `list<string>` - capabilities in the channel besides subscribing: "pub", "hst", "prs". Centrifugo PRO only.
- `$serverTagsFilter` `?FilterNode` - only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only.

### `Token`

Tokens: connection and subscription tokens for client SDKs, the JSON Web Key
Set Centrifugo verifies them with, and Centrifugo PRO's server API tokens.

```php
$key = Key::hmac($secret);   // client.token.hmac_secret_key
$token = Token::connection($key, new ConnectionClaims(
    user: '42',
    expiresAt: new DateTimeImmutable('+15 minutes'),
));
```

See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/authentication.

#### `static api(Key $key, ApiClaims $claims): string`

A token for Centrifugo PRO's server API with $claims, signed with $key -
an asymmetric key with an ID, published by jwks: Centrifugo PRO finds it
by the "kid". See ApiClaims for keeping it apart from client tokens, and
ApiTokens for one to send with every call.

#### `static connection(Key $key, ConnectionClaims $claims): string`

A connection token with $claims, signed with $key.

#### `static jwks(Key ...$keys): string`

The public keys of $keys as a JSON Web Key Set, for Centrifugo's
client.token.jwks_public_endpoint, which verifies tokens by their "kid".
Each key needs an ID - see Key::withKeyId - unique in the set. HMAC keys
have no public key to publish, and are refused, as is a set without
keys.

A set is how keys rotate without restarting Centrifugo: publish the new
key next to the old one; once every instance of the application
publishes it, sign with it; drop the old key once the tokens it signed
have expired. Never give a key ID to another key: Centrifugo caches keys
by ID.

Publish the keys of client tokens and of Centrifugo PRO's server API
tokens at separate endpoints: a token signed with any key of a set passes
Centrifugo's signature check.

#### `static subscription(Key $key, SubscriptionClaims $claims): string`

A subscription token with $claims, signed with $key.

## Centrifugal\Phpcent\Http

### `Handler`

```php
new Handler(?callable $onError, int $maxBody)
```

The base of every handler - a token or signature endpoint, the JWKS
endpoint, a proxy handler. Its framework-free core, handle, turns a request
into a response; handlePsr and psr15 serve it in PSR-7 and PSR-15 frameworks
(Slim, Mezzio, and Symfony or Laravel through their PSR-7 bridges), and
serve answers the request of a plain PHP script.

- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void`

#### `handle(
    string $method,
    array $headers = [],
    string $body = '',
    array $query = [],
    string $path = '',
    mixed $raw = null,
): HttpResponse`

Answers a request: the core every adapter calls. $raw is passed on to the
function as HttpRequest::$raw: the server's own request object, or what
your framework knows of the request, such as its authenticated user.

```php
// Laravel
Route::post('/centrifugo/connect', function (Request $request) use ($handler) {
    $res = $handler->handle($request->method(), $request->headers->all(), $request->getContent(), raw: $request->user());
    return response($res->body, $res->status, $res->headers);
});
```

#### `handlePsr(
    Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface $request,
    Psr\Http\Message\ResponseFactoryInterface&Psr\Http\Message\StreamFactoryInterface $factory,
): Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface`

Answers a PSR-7 request, with responses from $factory.

#### `psr15(
    Psr\Http\Message\ResponseFactoryInterface&Psr\Http\Message\StreamFactoryInterface $factory,
): Psr\Http\Server\RequestHandlerInterface`

The handler as a PSR-15 request handler, with responses from $factory:
new Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory(), say.

#### `serve(): void`

Answers the request of a plain PHP script - php-fpm, the built-in server -
from $_SERVER and php://input, sending the response with header() and
echo:

```php
// centrifugo_connect.php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';
$handler->serve();
```

### `HttpRequest`

```php
new HttpRequest(
    string $method,
    array $headers = [],
    array $query = [],
    string $path = '',
    mixed $raw = null,
)
```

A request to a handler, as the application's function receives it.

- `$method` `string` - the HTTP method, upper case
- `$headers` `array<string, string>` - the headers, names in lower case, values of a repeated header joined with ", ": those Centrifugo passes on from the client's connection to a proxy, the client SDK's to an endpoint
- `$query` `array<string, string>` - the query parameters
- `$path` `string` - the path, as the server saw it
- `$raw` `mixed` - the server's own form of the request - a PSR-7 ServerRequestInterface, $_SERVER, or what was given to handle - for what the core does not carry, such as the client's address or a user your framework authenticated

#### `header(string $name): ?string`

A header's value, looked up case-insensitively; null when absent.

### `HttpResponse`

```php
new HttpResponse(int $status, array $headers, string $body)
```

A handler's answer.

- `$headers` `array<string, string>`

## Centrifugal\Phpcent\Endpoints

### `ConnectionToken`

```php
new ConnectionToken(callable $issue, ?callable $onError = null)
```

The endpoint a client's getToken callback calls: $issue returns the
connection token of the request's user - from Token::connection, say - or
throws Unauthorized. It takes GET and POST, the body ignored.

```php
$endpoint = new ConnectionToken(function (HttpRequest $http) use ($key): string {
    $user = sessionUser($http->header('cookie')) ?? throw new Unauthorized();
    return Token::connection($key, new ConnectionClaims(
        user: $user,
        expiresAt: new DateTimeImmutable('+15 minutes'),
    ));
});
```

- `$issue` `callable(HttpRequest): string`
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void`

### `Jwks`

```php
new Jwks(Key ...$keys)
```

Serves the JSON Web Key Set of keys - see Token::jwks - at the URL configured
as Centrifugo's client.token.jwks_public_endpoint, or Centrifugo PRO's
http_api.jwks.endpoint for API keys. It answers GET and HEAD, cacheable for
five minutes. A set Token::jwks refuses fails here, when the endpoint is
built.

### `SharedPollSignature`

```php
new SharedPollSignature(callable $sign, ?callable $onError = null)
```

The endpoint a shared poll subscription's getSignature callback calls: a POST
of {"channel": ..., "keys": [...]}, answered {"signature": ..., "keys":
[...]}.

$sign decides which of the keys the user may track in the channel, signs
them - with SharedPoll::sign, say - and returns them, in the order signed,
with the signature: [$allowed, $signature]. The keys it leaves out are
revoked: the client stops tracking them. To end the subscription instead,
it throws Unauthorized. It may return only keys it was asked for: a
signature covering another would be refused, and such a key fails the
request with 500.

- `$sign` `callable(HttpRequest, string, list<string>): array{list<string>, string}`
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void`

### `SubscriptionToken`

```php
new SubscriptionToken(callable $issue, ?callable $onError = null)
```

The endpoint a subscription's getToken callback calls: $issue returns the
token of the request's user for the channel - from Token::subscription,
say - or throws Unauthorized when the user may not subscribe. The channel
comes from a POST's JSON body, {"channel": ...}, or from a GET's channel
query parameter; it is required.

- `$issue` `callable(HttpRequest, string): string`
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void`

### `Unauthorized`

```php
new Unauthorized(string $message = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

Thrown by the function of an endpoint when the user may not have a token or
signature: answered with 403, on which client SDKs stop asking. It is the
endpoints' own, named after client SDKs' UnauthorizedError - not the API
client's UnauthorizedException, which means Centrifugo refused the SDK's
credentials.

## Centrifugal\Phpcent\Proxy

### `ConnectHandler`

```php
new ConnectHandler(callable $func, ?callable $onError = null, int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY)
```

The connect proxy: the function authenticates a connecting client and returns
its user and initial state. ProxyError rejects the connection; Disconnect
closes it with that code.

```php
$handler = new ConnectHandler(function (ConnectRequest $req, HttpRequest $http): ConnectResult {
    $user = sessionUser($http->header('cookie'))   // passed on with http_headers
        ?? throw new Disconnect(4501, 'unauthorized');
    return new ConnectResult(user: $user);
});
```

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `Disconnect`

```php
new Disconnect(int $code, string $reason = '', ?Throwable $previous = null)
```

Thrown by a proxy function to close the client's connection: a code in
[4000, 4999] - [4000, 4499] tells the client to reconnect, [4500, 4999] not
to. $reason is a short description, at most 32 bytes.

### `MapPublishHandler`

```php
new MapPublishHandler(
    callable $func,
    ?callable $onError = null,
    int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY,
)
```

The map publish proxy: the function decides whether a client may publish a
key into a map channel, and may change the publication.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `MapRemoveHandler`

```php
new MapRemoveHandler(
    callable $func,
    ?callable $onError = null,
    int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY,
)
```

The map remove proxy: the function decides whether a client may remove a key
from a map channel.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `NotifyCacheEmptyHandler`

```php
new NotifyCacheEmptyHandler(
    callable $func,
    ?callable $onError = null,
    int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY,
)
```

The cache empty proxy of Centrifugo PRO: the function learns that a client
subscribed to a channel in cache recovery mode with nothing to recover, and
may publish the current state - then it returns a result with populated set,
for Centrifugo to recover once more. Any exception fails the request, and the
client which subscribed is disconnected to reconnect.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `NotifyChannelStateHandler`

```php
new NotifyChannelStateHandler(
    callable $func,
    ?callable $onError = null,
    int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY,
)
```

The channel state proxy of Centrifugo PRO, in preview: the function receives
channels becoming occupied or vacated. ProxyError, or any other exception,
fails the request.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `ProxyError`

```php
new ProxyError(
    int $code,
    string $message = '',
    bool $temporary = false,
    ?Throwable $previous = null,
)
```

Thrown by a proxy function to reject the client's request with this error:
a code in [400, 1999], which Centrifugo leaves to applications. $temporary
tells the client that retrying may succeed.

### `ProxyHandler`

```php
new ProxyHandler(callable $func, ?callable $onError = null, int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY)
```

The application side of a Centrifugo HTTP proxy: it decodes the request
Centrifugo sends, calls the function, and encodes its answer.

Answering: the function returns a result to accept the request, or throws:

- ProxyError rejects the request with that error, which the client
  receives: use codes in [400, 1999]. The connect, subscribe, publish, RPC,
  map publish and map remove proxies pass it to the client; the shared poll
  refresh and channel state proxies take it as a failure.
- Disconnect closes the client's connection with that code: use codes in
  [4000, 4999] - [4500, 4999] to tell the client not to reconnect. Only the
  proxies which pass a ProxyError to the client honour it.
- Any other exception, or one a proxy cannot carry, fails the request with
  HTTP status 500, and is passed to onError for logging. Centrifugo then
  answers the client with its temporary internal error; for refresh and sub
  refresh it keeps the connection or subscription for another minute and
  asks again.

A ProxyError or Disconnect as the previous exception of another counts too.
The refresh and sub refresh proxies end a connection or subscription through
their result's expired, not an exception.

Payloads - data, info, meta - arrive as json_decode gives them, objects as
stdClass, and a result takes them back as they are, or as RawJson. A proxy
with binary_encoding enabled sends them base64-encoded in the b64 fields,
with encoding "binary"; a result may answer with either field.

Security: Centrifugo trusts what a proxy endpoint answers, and the endpoint
trusts what Centrifugo sends - a SubscribeRequest's user is the user
Centrifugo authenticated. Anyone else able to reach the endpoint could claim
any user. Keep proxy endpoints reachable by Centrifugo only: on an internal
network, or behind a check of a secret Centrifugo sends as a static header.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `PublishHandler`

```php
new PublishHandler(callable $func, ?callable $onError = null, int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY)
```

The publish proxy: the function decides whether a client may publish into a
channel, and may change the publication. ProxyError rejects it; Disconnect
closes the connection.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `RefreshHandler`

```php
new RefreshHandler(callable $func, ?callable $onError = null, int $maxBody = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BODY)
```

The refresh proxy: the function decides whether a connection about to expire
lives on, and until when. To end it, return a result with expired set. Any
exception fails the request, and Centrifugo keeps the connection for another
minute before asking again.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

### `RpcHandler`


The RPC proxy: the function answers a client's RPC call. ProxyError fails the
call; Disconnect closes the connection.

- `$func` `callable(TRequest, HttpRequest): TResult` - answers the proxy request: it takes the decoded request and the HTTP request - with the headers Centrifugo passed on
- `$onError` `?callable(HttpRequest, \Throwable): void` - told of every 500 and 400, with the exception

#### `FilterNode`

```php
new FilterNode(
    string $op = '',
    string $key = '',
    string $cmp = '',
    string $val = '',
    array $vals = [],
    array $nodes = [],
)
```

FilterNode is a tree describing a predicate over client labels. Used as
$labelFilter on Subscribe, Unsubscribe, Disconnect, Refresh and
Connections requests. A node is either a leaf comparison (key, cmp, val or
vals) or a logical operation (op) over child nodes.
Centrifugo PRO only: defined here for protocol-surface consistency,
Centrifugo OSS parses it but ignores it.

- `$op` `string` - The logical operation of a non-leaf node: "and", "or" or "not". Empty for a leaf node.
- `$key` `string` - The label key a leaf node compares.
- `$cmp` `string` - The comparison of a leaf node: "eq", "neq", "in", "nin", "ex", "nex", "sw", "ew", "ct", "gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte".
- `$val` `string` - The value to compare with, for single-value comparisons.
- `$vals` `list<string>` - The values to compare with, for "in" and "nin".
- `$nodes` `list<FilterNode>` - The child nodes of a logical operation.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `ChannelEvent`

```php
new ChannelEvent(int $timeMs = 0, string $channel = '', string $type = '')
```

ChannelEvent is a change of a channel's state.

- `$timeMs` `int` - When it happened, in Unix milliseconds.
- `$channel` `string` - The channel it happened in.
- `$type` `string` - "occupied" when the channel got its first subscriber, "vacated" when it lost its last one. More types may come; the field is a string, not an enum, for JSON interoperability.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `ChannelsCapability`

```php
new ChannelsCapability(array $channels = [], array $allow = [], string $match = '')
```

ChannelsCapability grants operations in channels. A connection may do an
operation in a channel when any of its capabilities both allows the
operation and matches the channel. Centrifugo PRO only.

- `$channels` `list<string>` - The channels, or channel patterns, it applies to.
- `$allow` `list<string>` - The operations it grants: "sub" (subscribe), "pub" (publish), "hst" (history) and "prs" (presence).
- `$match` `string` - How channels are matched: empty for exact names, "wildcard" or "regex".

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `ConnectRequest`

```php
new ConnectRequest(
    string $client = '',
    string $transport = '',
    string $protocol = '',
    string $encoding = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    string $name = '',
    string $version = '',
    array $channels = [],
)
```

ConnectRequest is sent when a client connects.

- `$client` `string` - The unique ID Centrifugo gave the connection.
- `$transport` `string` - The connection's transport: "websocket", "sse", "uni_sse" and the like.
- `$protocol` `string` - The client protocol: "json" or "protobuf".
- `$encoding` `string` - "binary" when the proxy has binary_encoding enabled, so that payloads come in the b64 fields, and "json" otherwise.
- `$data` `mixed` - The custom data the client sent with its connect command, if any.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, sent instead of data in binary encoding mode.
- `$name` `string` - The client's name, if it sent one.
- `$version` `string` - The client's version, if it sent one.
- `$channels` `list<string>` - The server-side channels the client asks to be subscribed to. The backend checks its permissions and returns the allowed ones in ConnectResult::$channels or ConnectResult::$subs.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `ConnectResult`

```php
new ConnectResult(
    string $user = '',
    int $expireAt = 0,
    mixed $info = null,
    string $b64info = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    array $channels = [],
    array $subs = [],
    mixed $meta = null,
    array $caps = [],
    array $labels = [],
)
```

ConnectResult accepts the connection.

- `$user` `string` - The ID of the user the connection belongs to. Empty accepts an anonymous connection.
- `$expireAt` `int` - When the connection expires, in Unix seconds, unless refreshed - by the refresh proxy, when one is configured. Zero means it does not expire.
- `$info` `mixed` - Information about the connection, as JSON: it is part of presence data, join and leave events and the client's publications.
- `$b64info` `string` - Info in base64, for binary info.
- `$data` `mixed` - Custom data sent to the client in the connect reply.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, for binary data.
- `$channels` `list<string>` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to.
- `$subs` `array<string, SubscribeOptions>` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to, each with its options.
- `$meta` `mixed` - Custom data attached to the connection, as JSON. It is never sent to the client; proxies with include_connection_meta receive it.
- `$caps` `list<ChannelsCapability>` - Capabilities granting the connection operations in channels. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `$labels` `array<string, string>` - PRO only — client labels attached to the centrifuge.Client by Centrifugo PRO. Parsed by OSS but not used (OSS does not populate centrifuge.ConnectReply.Labels).

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `FilterNode`

```php
new FilterNode(
    string $op = '',
    string $key = '',
    string $cmp = '',
    string $val = '',
    array $vals = [],
    array $nodes = [],
)
```

FilterNode is a node of a publication tags filter expression. A leaf node
compares one tag: it sets key, cmp and val or vals, and leaves op empty. A
logical node combines its nodes: it sets op and nodes only.

- `$op` `string` - The logical operation: "and", "or" or "not". Empty for a leaf node.
- `$key` `string` - The tag a leaf node compares.
- `$cmp` `string` - The comparison of a leaf node: "eq", "neq", "in", "nin", "ex" (exists), "nex" (does not exist), "sw" (starts with), "ew" (ends with), "ct" (contains), "gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte".
- `$val` `string` - The value most comparisons compare the tag with.
- `$vals` `list<string>` - The values "in" and "nin" compare the tag with.
- `$nodes` `list<FilterNode>` - The operands of a logical node.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

```php
new MapPublishRequest(
    string $client = '',

    string $channel = '',
    string $key = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    mixed $meta = null,

)
```

MapPublishRequest is sent when a client publishes a key into a map channel.

- `$client` `string` - The unique ID Centrifugo gave the connection.
- `$transport` `string` - The connection's transport.
- `$protocol` `string` - The client protocol: "json" or "protobuf".
- `$encoding` `string` - "binary" when the proxy has binary_encoding enabled, so that payloads come in the b64 fields, and "json" otherwise.
- `$user` `string` - The connection's user ID.
- `$channel` `string` - The map channel the client publishes into.
- `$key` `string` - The key the client publishes, empty if it sent none.
- `$data` `mixed` - The data the client publishes.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, sent instead of data in binary encoding mode.
- `$meta` `mixed` - The connection's meta, when the proxy has include_connection_meta.
- `$labels` `array<string, string>` - PRO only — connection labels attached to the originating centrifuge.Client. Centrifugo PRO always populates this from Client.Labels() (no opt-in toggle).

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `MapPublishResult`

```php
new MapPublishResult(
    string $key = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    array $tags = [],
    int $score = 0,
    string $keyMode = '',
    mixed $streamData = null,
    string $b64streamData = '',
    string $idempotencyKey = '',
    bool $delta = false,
    int $version = 0,
    string $versionEpoch = '',
)
```

MapPublishResult accepts the publication, even when empty. Fields left
unset keep what the client sent, or the defaults.

- `$key` `string` - Replaces the key the client sent: to force a key the server derives, such as the user ID.
- `$data` `mixed` - Replaces the data the client sent.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, for binary data.
- `$tags` `array<string, string>` - Attached to the publication: clients cannot send tags, so this is where server-side tag filters get their tags from.
- `$score` `int` - Not used by Centrifugo yet.
- `$keyMode` `string` - Makes the publication conditional: "if_new" publishes only a key which does not exist yet, "if_exists" only one which does.
- `$streamData` `mixed` - Not used by Centrifugo yet.
- `$b64streamData` `string` - Not used by Centrifugo yet.
- `$idempotencyKey` `string` - Makes the publication idempotent: another one with the same key within the broker's idempotency window is not published.
- `$delta` `bool` - Enables delta compression for the publication.
- `$version` `int` - The key's version: Centrifugo drops a publication older than the key's latest.
- `$versionEpoch` `string` - Scopes version, for versions which may start over.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `PublishResult`

```php
new PublishResult(

```

PublishResult accepts the publication. Fields left unset keep what the
client sent, or the defaults.

- `$data` `mixed` - Replaces the data the client sent.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, for binary data.
- `$skipHistory` `bool` - Publishes without saving the publication to the channel's history. Not allowed in channels with delta compression.
- `$tags` `array<string, string>` - Attached to the publication: clients cannot send tags, so this is where server-side tag filters get their tags from.
- `$idempotencyKey` `string` - Makes the publication idempotent: another one with the same key in the channel within the broker's idempotency window is not published.
- `$delta` `bool` - Enables delta compression for the publication.
- `$version` `int` - The publication's version, for channels whose publications each carry the whole state: Centrifugo drops one older than the latest.
- `$versionEpoch` `string` - Scopes version, for versions which may start over - when they come from a system which can lose its state, say.

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `SharedPollRefreshResult`

```php
new SharedPollRefreshResult(array $items = [], string $epoch = '')
```

SharedPollRefreshResult carries the items' current data. An item left out
is unchanged.

- `$items` `list<SharedPollRefreshResultItem>` - The items' current data.
- `$epoch` `string` - Identifies the publisher's version space: when it differs from the channel's, Centrifugo drops the versions and data it keeps and resubscribes the channel's subscribers. Generate one per process start, and send the same one with direct publishes. Empty means versions are never reset.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `SharedPollRefreshResultItem`

```php
new SharedPollRefreshResultItem(
    string $key = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    int $version = 0,
    bool $removed = false,
    mixed $prevData = null,
)
```

SharedPollRefreshResultItem is an item's current data.

- `$key` `string` - The item's key.
- `$data` `mixed` - The item's data. In versioned mode it may be left out for an item which has not changed.
- `$version` `int` - The item's version: required in versioned mode, optional in versionless mode. It must grow when the item changes.
- `$removed` `bool` - Removes the item: subscribers are told so, and it is no longer tracked.
- `$prevData` `mixed` - The item's previous data, the base for delta compression when the namespace uses it, so that Centrifugo need not keep it.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

#### `SubscribeOptions`

```php
new SubscribeOptions(
    int $expireAt = 0,
    mixed $info = null,
    string $b64info = '',
    mixed $data = null,
    string $b64data = '',
    ?SubscribeOptionOverride $override = null,
    ?FilterNode $serverTagsFilter = null,
    bool $cacheRecover = false,
)
```

SubscribeOptions are the options of a server-side subscription returned in
ConnectResult::$subs.

- `$expireAt` `int` - When the subscription expires, in Unix seconds. Zero means it does not expire.
- `$info` `mixed` - Channel-specific information about the connection, as JSON: it is part of presence data, join and leave events and the client's publications in the channel.
- `$b64info` `string` - Info in base64, for binary info.
- `$data` `mixed` - Custom data sent to the client with the subscription in the connect reply.
- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, for binary data.
- `$override` `SubscribeOptionOverride|null` - Overrides channel options of the namespace for this subscription.
- `$serverTagsFilter` `FilterNode|null` - Makes the subscription receive only publications whose tags match it. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `$cacheRecover` `bool` - When set, makes Centrifugo initiate cache recovery for the server-side subscription without requiring the client to provide a recover flag/position itself. This is the server-side equivalent of subscribing with an empty `since` on the client. Mostly useful for unidirectional clients which do not know channel names. Requires recovery to be enabled for the channel and only applies in cache recovery mode, where it delivers the latest publication on (re)subscribe.

##### `toJson(string $path = ''): string`

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.

- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, sent instead of data in binary encoding mode.


SubscribeResult accepts the subscription.

- `$b64data` `string` - Data in base64, for binary data.
- `$override` `SubscribeOptionOverride|null` - Overrides channel options of the namespace for this subscription.
- `$allow` `list<string>` - Capabilities granted in the channel for this subscription: "sub", "pub", "hst" and "prs". Centrifugo PRO only.
- `$serverTagsFilter` `FilterNode|null` - Makes the subscription receive only publications whose tags match it. Centrifugo PRO only.

The message as Centrifugo reads it: JSON, fields at their zero value
left out. $path prefixes the field names in error messages.
